proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 03:58 UTC on 19 August. The content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published, meaning the pipeline is almost empty and a broken publish workflow will create a content gap that directly reduces organic traffic and new list entries. This is the highest-leverage fix because content is the primary top-of-funnel driver.
proposals.proposal:
Inspect the workflow run logs for the Daily Blog Post action, identify the failure cause (likely an expired API token, a changed environment variable name, or a schema mismatch after the recent cash-flow engine syncs), and apply a one-line fix to the workflow file or its corresponding secret reference. Do not touch .github/workflows/* paths that are blocked. Because .github/workflows/daily-blog-post.yml is listed as blocked, Joel must apply this fix manually in the GitHub UI or via a direct commit outside Fred's write scope. Fred's role here is to surface the exact diagnostic so Joel can act in under ten minutes.

Check these three things in order: (1) whether the OPENAI_API_KEY or MAILERLITE_API_KEY secret has rotated since the last successful run, (2) whether the blog post schema expects a field that the cash-flow engine sync commits (sha 6354e41, 59a67b0) may have added or removed from content.config.ts, (3) whether the queued post file itself has a malformed frontmatter date.

The fix is one of: refresh the secret in GitHub Settings, revert a field name in the queued post's frontmatter, or pin the schema version the workflow uses.

proposals.observation: The Funnel-Hack Digest workflow also failed, at 09:16 UTC on the same day. Two workflow failures on one day, both after the cash-flow engine sync commits, suggests the syncs introduced a shared breaking change, probably in an environment variable or a shared utility the workflows both call. Fixing the digest restores whatever competitive-intelligence or nurture content Joel uses internally, and prevents a second silent gap.
proposals.proposal:
After fixing the Daily Blog Post workflow (Proposal 1), re-run the Funnel-Hack Digest workflow without changes first. If it passes, the root cause was a transient API timeout. If it fails again with the same error, the two workflows share a broken dependency, and the fix applied in Proposal 1 needs to be mirrored here. Joel should check the failed run's annotation in the Actions tab: if the error message is identical to the blog workflow's, one fix resolves both.

The concrete action: open the Funnel-Hack Digest failed run in GitHub Actions, copy the error text, compare it to the Daily Blog Post error text. Identical errors mean one secret or one utility file is the root cause. Apply the same fix. Different errors mean two separate issues, and the digest failure is lower priority than the blog gap.

proposals.impact: lift 37.5% open rate toward Money Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate across 16 sends, compared to Money Vigilance at 66.67% (12 sends) and Money Avoidance at 52.63% (19 sends). Money Worship is the lowest-performing sequence by a clear margin. Subject line quality is the single highest-leverage variable at the email level because it determines whether the rest of the sequence is read at all. The first email's subject line is the right place to start because it sets the open-rate tone for the whole automation.
proposals.proposal:
Rewrite the subject line of the first email in the Money Worship automation. The current line is almost certainly a statement about money and worth, or a question framed around "deserving" — the standard Money Worship archetype framing that every financial-coaching account runs. The replacement needs to pass the Sultanic test: something only Joel could write, grounded in a specific moment rather than a category description.

The new subject line should name the quiet, specific feeling that money worship produces in a person's week — not the belief system, the actual texture of Tuesday morning when they've just refreshed their bank balance twice and still don't feel settled. That is the thing the reader recognises before they recognise the label.
proposals.current_text: subject: "Your money says a lot about your worth — let's change that"
proposals.new_text: subject: "You checked your balance three times this morning and still felt behind"
